claim: On November 20, 2024 Kinesis Data Streams on-demand mode started to scale to streams that write up to 10GB/s per stream and consumers that read up to 20 GB/s per stream, a 5x increase from the previous limits of 2 GB/s for writers and 4 GB/s for readers.
question: What was the on-demand write and read throughput limit of a Kinesis data stream before November 2024?

qualifiers.condition: the 10 GB/s limit holds in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon) and Europe (Ireland); other Regions are lower

evidence.quote: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams On-Demand Mode now automatically scales to support streaming applications that write up to 10GB/s per stream and consumers that read up to 20 GB/s per stream. This is a 5x increase from the previously supported limits of 2 GB/s per stream for writers and 4 GB/s for readers.

note: Current truth: kinesis-data-streams-on-demand-max-throughput-regions. Older exam questions may assume 200 MB/s.

claim: On October 30, 2023 Kinesis Data Streams on-demand mode could be raised through AWS Support to scale up to 2 GB/s write and 4 GB/s read throughput. Before that, on-demand mode scaled by default up to 200MB/s write and 400MB/s read, and earlier in 2023 the limit was raised to 1 GB/s write and 2GB/s read.
question: How did the on-demand throughput limit of Kinesis Data Streams change during 2023?

qualifiers.condition: later raised again to 10 GB/s in November 2024

evidence.quote: By default, On-Demand mode can automatically scale up to 200MB/s write and 400MB/s read throughput. Earlier in the year, we increased this limit up to 1 GB/s write and 2GB/s read throughput. As we continue to innovate to provide more powerful streaming capabilities, you can now request a limit increase through AWS Support to enable your On-Demand stream to scale up to 2 GB/s write and 4 GB/s read throughput.
